Zadok
ZAY-dok
proper noun
Hebrew Tsadoq, “righteous” or “just,” the faithful high priest under David and Solomon.

Biblical Definition

Zadok was the faithful high priest in the days of David and Solomon, whose name fitly means “righteous.” When Absalom drove David from Jerusalem, Zadok and the Levites bore the ark out of the city to follow the king, until David sent them back to keep it in its place (2Sa 15:24). When Adonijah sought the throne, Zadok stood with the rightful succession, and it was he who took the horn of oil out of the tabernacle and anointed Solomon, while all the people cried, God save king Solomon (1Ki 1:39). For this fidelity his house was confirmed in the priesthood, and the prophet Ezekiel honoured the sons of Zadok, the priests the Levites that kept the charge of God’s sanctuary when the children of Israel went astray, as those who should come near to minister unto the LORD (Eze 44:15). The dictionary marks Zadok as the pattern of the faithful priest. His loyalty in the day of revolt, and the steadiness of his house through the apostasies of Israel, made him a figure of the faithful priest the LORD promised to raise up, who should do according to that which is in His heart and mind, walking before His anointed for ever (1Sa 2:35). That promise found its full answer in Christ, the great High Priest, of whose unfailing faithfulness Zadok was a shadow.

Webster 1828 Definition

The faithful high priest under David and Solomon, who anointed Solomon and whose house kept the priesthood.

ZADOK, the faithful high priest under David and Solomon.

His name fitly means “righteous” or “just.”

He bore the ark for David during Absalom’s revolt.

He anointed Solomon king against Adonijah’s usurpation.

Ezekiel honoured the sons of Zadok who kept the charge of the sanctuary.

Key Scripture

1Ki 1:39 — "And Zadok the priest took an horn of oil out of the tabernacle, and anointed Solomon. And they blew the trumpet; and all the people said, God save king Solomon."

Eze 44:15 — "But the priests the Levites, the sons of Zadok, that kept the charge of my sanctuary when the children of Israel went astray from me, they shall come near to me to minister unto me, and they shall stand before me to offer unto me the fat and the blood, saith the Lord GOD:"

2Sa 15:24 — "And lo Zadok also, and all the Levites were with him, bearing the ark of the covenant of God: and they set down the ark of God; and Abiathar went up, until all the people had done passing out of the city."

1Sa 2:35 — "And I will raise me up a faithful priest, that shall do according to that which is in mine heart and in my mind: and I will build him a sure house; and he shall walk before mine anointed for ever."

Modern Corruption

A figure of Scripture; the faithful priest Zadok is a shadow of Christ, the great High Priest who never fails.

expand to see more

Zadok has drawn no redefinition from the present age, surviving as the faithful priest of David’s and Solomon’s day. The dictionary records him that the reader may mark the loyalty and steadiness for which the Scripture honours him and his house.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the faithful priesthood. Zadok stood with the rightful king in the day of revolt, anointed Solomon, and kept the charge of the sanctuary when Israel went astray; and his house was confirmed in the priesthood for its fidelity. He is a figure of the faithful priest the LORD promised to raise up, who should do all His will and walk before His anointed for ever. That promise is fulfilled in Christ, the great High Priest, of whose unfailing faithfulness Zadok was but a shadow; and the believer rests not in any earthly priest but in Him.

Hebrew Roots

From the Hebrew for “righteous,” Zadok names the faithful high priest under David and Solomon.

"Like Zadok, the faithful priest stands with the rightful King in the day of revolt."

"Zadok anointed Solomon, and all the people said, God save king Solomon."

"The faithful priest is a shadow of Christ, the great High Priest who never fails."
